relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan. It exhibits an infinite family of Montesinos knots (the pretzel knot P(5,-3,5) and the family C(5,-3,5,u)) whose first colored Jones coefficient grows LINEARLY in the colour n, so the stability phenomenon known for alternating knots and the resulting 'tail' does not generalize naively; the authors name these Manx knots. This is a clean counterexample result, and I looked for a corpus claim it would bear on. Corpus-grep: content/ has no claim of stability or boundedness of colored Jones coefficients; the folio's colored-Jones-adjacent claims are conj:three-knot-jet-order-independence (which uses the Habiro cyclotomic expansion, a different grading that exists for all knots and is untouched by tail failure) and conj:b1-hyperbolic-rows-theorem (which uses Volume-Conjecture asymptotics, not coefficient stability). Also none of the Manx knots is in the folio's knot inventory, which is torus knots plus 4_1 plus the Borromean rings. So the counterexample has nothing here to counter. Scope-(a): as read, supplies nothing usable — this is not a claim that tail/stability phenomena are irrelevant to the folio, only that no current block depends on them. Note: one author is already registered for a different paper (vanderveen2008, cited from two Lean files), so an automated author match on this file would be a false positive.

proposedActions.rationale: No folio block assumes stability of colored Jones coefficients or uses tails, and the Manx family is not in the folio's knot inventory; there is no target for the counterexample.
